pulses.name: Suspected DPRK Campaign staging PHP2Shell Targeting against Global PHP infrastructure
pulses.description: A Korean-speaking threat actor, tracked as the June 2026 Minjun campaign and linked with moderate confidence to North Korea's Lazarus Group, is actively planning targeted exploitation of two critical PHP vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) that enable unauthenticated remote code execution. The campaign prioritizes government agencies, financial institutions, manufacturing, logistics, aviation, and trading platforms across the US, Japan, Thailand, Indonesia, Korea, Australia, Taiwan, India, Singapore, UAE, Saudi Arabia, and the EU. Operators are using AI-assisted reconnaissance to rank public exploit code and plan sector-specific attacks. Exploitation attempts have been observed globally since 17 October 2026, with 17 suspected source IPs identified conducting web shell deployment and session poisoning. The vulnerabilities affect all internet-facing PHP installations below version 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, or 8.2.35, with Apache mod_php at highest risk.

pulses.description: On October 23, PHP released an informational advisory disclosing another remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2026-115560). The advisory states that the issue requires “an unusual combination of configuration and application code” and that mitigations published for PHP2Shell vulnerability CVE-2026-109619 also address this threat. indicators.content:
rule PHP2Shell_Request_Shape_In_Capture    
   {    
   meta:    
   description = "PHP2Shell scanner/PoC strings or exploit request shape in captured HTTP requests"    
   author = "CYFIRMA Research"    
   date = "2026-10-22"    
   category = "Threat Hunting"    
   severity = "Medium"    
   scan_scope = "Per-request captures: ModSecurity audit log entries, WAF/proxy body dumps, PCAP-extracted bodies. Counts aggregate across the whole file, so do not run the shape branch on multi-request logs"    
   note = "UA, boundary and marker strings come from honeypot and community reporting of public tooling and are trivially changed. JACKALPOC in a captured response (not request) indicates the validation command ran. The upload-progress field name is configurable (session.upload_progress.name)"    
   strings:    
   $ua1 = "php2shell-scan" ascii nocase    
   $ua2 = "php2shell-verify" ascii nocase    
   $ua3 = /php2shell-1096[0-9]{2}/ ascii nocase    
   $bnd1 = "-p2s" ascii    
   $bnd2 = "B7kQpoc619" ascii    
   $marker = "JACKALPOC" ascii    
   $field = "PHP_SESSION_UPLOAD_PROGRESS" ascii    
   $empty_file = "filename=\"\"" ascii    
   $array_part = /name="[A-Za-z0-9_]{1,32}\[\]"/ ascii    
   condition:    
   filesize < 20MB and    
   (    
   any of ($ua*, $bnd*, $marker) or    
   ($field and #empty_file >= 10) or    
   ($field and #array_part >= 100)    
   )    
   }

indicators.content:
rule PHP2Shell_Log_Crash_Signatures    
   {    
   meta:    
   description = "PHP error-log and PHP-FPM log lines consistent with PHP2Shell trigger attempts (pre-request OOM, session decode failure, worker segfault)"    
   author = "CYFIRMA Research"    
   date = "2026-10-22"    
   category = "Threat Hunting"    
   severity = "Low"    
   note = "Side-effect indicators, not proof of exploitation. Derived from community lab testing (largely PHP CLI server; nginx/FPM/Apache mappings provisional). Correlate with multipart POSTs from the same source. A memory-limit fatal with memory_limit=-1 set is a strong signal"    
   strings:    
   $oom = /Allowed memory size of [0-9]{1,12} bytes exhausted[^\n]{0,200} in Unknown on line 0/ ascii    
   $decode = "Failed to decode session object" ascii    
   $segv = "exited on signal 11 (SIGSEGV)" ascii    
   condition:    
   $oom or ($decode and $segv)    
   }

pulses.name: Hunting Leaked PHP2Shell RCE Across Open Directories (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619)
pulses.description: Two critical PHP remote code execution vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, both rated CVSS v4.0 9.2, leaked before their scheduled patch on October 21, 2026. The flaws involve out-of-memory corruption in PHP core through multipart/form-data parsing, exploitable via session.upload_progress without authentication. Scanning began approximately 20 minutes after the patch release, with activity traced to a Mirai-style IoT botnet. Analysis of attacker infrastructure revealed approximately ten workspaces staging php2shell tooling, targeting WooCommerce, WHMCS, and Magento platforms. Despite widespread exposure affecting over 683,000 IPs running vulnerable PHP versions, no successful in-the-wild exploitation was confirmed as of October 21, 2026. The technical difficulty of achieving reliable code execution on systems with address-space randomization limited successful compromises.

pulses.name: Amazon Threat Intelligence identifies PHP2Shell exploitation prior to public disclosure in MadPot
pulses.description: Amazon Threat Intelligence discovered PHP2Shell exploitation attempts in MadPot honeypot telemetry on October 17, 2026, four days before the public disclosure of CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. The initial exploit originated from a commercial anonymization network, suggesting threat actor involvement during the embargo period. Multiple proof-of-concept exploits emerged on the disclosure date, with varied payloads and infrastructure indicating multiple actors. Following the embargo lift on October 21, 2026, exploitation became widespread within hours. This incident highlights two critical lessons: coordinated disclosure cannot guarantee zero-day protection, and AI-assisted analysis has dramatically shortened the time from patch release to working exploits, requiring organizations to measure patch timelines in hours rather than days.

pulses.name: PHP2Shell Vulnerabilities: CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619
pulses.description: Two critical remote code execution vulnerabilities in PHP, collectively named PHP2Shell, were disclosed on October 21, 2026. CVE-2026-109618 involves out-of-memory handling corruption that can interrupt PHP while internal request data is partially initialized, leading to invalid data treatment. CVE-2026-109619 exploits stale global state where request-owned internal state survives after memory is freed. Both vulnerabilities can be exploited successfully on ARM64 systems and x86 systems without ASLR. Fixed versions include PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35. Over 2.6 million internet-facing hosts running PHP were identified as vulnerable, with 42% on end-of-life branches receiving no official patches. Early exploitation attempts were observed from multiple sources, including scanning activity and webshell deployment attempts targeting the upload-progress vulnerability path.
